Class LifeHistoryInvariantsEngine

java.lang.Object
org.ether.society.core.engine.AbstractSimulationEngine
org.ether.society.engines.tier1.LifeHistoryInvariantsEngine
All Implemented Interfaces:
SimulationEngineModule
public class LifeHistoryInvariantsEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine
Universal Life-History Invariants & Demographic Allocation Engine.

Formalizes the dimensionless evolutionary symmetries and life-history optimization established by Eric L. Charnov (1991, 1993, Life History Invariants, Oxford Univ. Press), Stephen C. Stearns (1992), and Promislow & Harvey (1990).

Key Bioenergetic & Evolutionary Mechanics:

  1. Charnov's Dimensionless Symmetry (\(M \cdot \alpha = C_{\text{charnov}}\)): Across mammalian taxa and human populations, the dimensionless product of adult mortality hazard \(\mu_{\text{adult}}\) and age at reproductive maturity \(\alpha\) is an evolutionary invariant: \[ \mu_{\text{adult}} \cdot \alpha = C_{\text{charnov}} \approx 1.80 \pm 0.20 \] linking extrinsic environmental hazard directly to reproductive ontogeny.
  2. Optimal Reproductive Maturity Age (\(\alpha^*\)): Under fluctuating extrinsic mortality \(\mu_{\text{total}} = \mu_{\text{ext}} + \mu_{\text{intrinsic}}\): \[ \alpha^*(\mu) = \frac{C_{\text{charnov}}}{\mu_{\text{total}}} \quad [\text{years}] \] bounded by somatic physiological constraints (\(\alpha \in [\alpha_{\min}, \alpha_{\max}]\)). High-mortality paleolithic or crisis conditions accelerate maturation ("fast" life-history strategy), whereas safe, low-mortality environments lengthen juvenile investment and somatic encephalization.
  3. Juvenile Survivorship & Parental Allocation: Survival probability from birth to maturity \(\alpha\): \[ l_\alpha = \exp(-\mu_{\text{juv}} \cdot \alpha) \] where juvenile mortality scales proportionally to adult environmental hazard: \(\mu_{\text{juv}} = q_{\text{juv}} \cdot \mu_{\text{adult}}\).
  4. Adaptive Reproductive Effort & Fertility Rate (\(b^*\)): At demographic replacement equilibrium (\(R_0 = l_\alpha \cdot \frac{b}{\mu} \approx 1.0\)), the equilibrium fertility rate per reproductive female balances mortality: \[ b^*(\mu) = \frac{\mu_{\text{adult}}}{l_\alpha} = \mu_{\text{adult}} \cdot \exp(q_{\text{juv}} \cdot C_{\text{charnov}}) \]

  • Method Details

    • calculateOptimalReproductiveAge

      public static double calculateOptimalReproductiveAge(double adultMortalityRate)
      Calculates the optimal age at reproductive maturity \(\alpha^*\) in years based on total adult mortality hazard \(\mu\): \[ \alpha^*(\mu) = \text{clamp}\left(\frac{C_{\text{charnov}}}{\mu}, \; \alpha_{\min}, \; \alpha_{\max}\right) \]
      Parameters:
      adultMortalityRate - annual instantaneous adult mortality hazard (\(\text{yr}^{-1}\))
      Returns:
      optimal age at first reproduction in years

    • calculateJuvenileSurvivorship

      public static double calculateJuvenileSurvivorship(double adultMortalityRate, double reproductiveAgeYears)

      Parameters:
      adultMortalityRate - annual adult mortality hazard (\(\text{yr}^{-1}\))
      reproductiveAgeYears - age at maturity in years
      Returns:
      survival probability \(l_\alpha \in (0, 1]\)

      public static double calculateEquilibriumBirthRate(double adultMortalityRate, double juvenileSurvivorship)
